name: HM-2807 1300KV outrunner motor
summary: A 28 by 7 mm stator outrunner for 7-inch multirotors on 6S. Sample data: the supplier and every figure here are fictional.

evidence.summary: Supplier datasheet and material documents received.
checked: Datasheet part number matches the sample label
Rated KV, stator size and cell rating as stated by the supplier
Magnet grade and wire class as stated on supplier certificates
notChecked: Whether the stated figures hold across production batches

evidence.summary: One production sample measured on our bench.
checked: KV, mass, phase resistance and shaft diameter on one sample
Slot and pole count, by counting
notChecked: More than one sample, so no batch spread

evidence.summary: Final assembly seen on site at the supplier.
checked: Stator winding and final assembly take place at the Coimbatore site
Bell housings are machined on site
notChecked: Where the stator laminations are cut
Where the lead wire is made

measurements.label: Production steps observed
measurements.value: Winding, magnet bonding, bell machining, final assembly

evidence.summary: Thrust and current measured by an outside lab.
checked: Thrust, current and efficiency from 10 to 100 percent throttle
One motor, one 7x4 propeller, bench supply at 25.2 V

parts.name: Mounting base
parts.role: Bolts the motor to the frame arm and holds the stator still.
parts.whatItDoes: The base is the fixed half of the motor. Four threaded holes take the screws that hold the motor to the arm, and a centre tube carries the stator and both bearings.
parts.whyItMatters: A base that flexes or is machined off-centre lets the rotor wobble, which shows up as vibration in the flight controller and as wear in the bearings.
buyingChecks: Mounting pattern matches your arm, usually 16 x 16 or 19 x 19 mm
Screw length: screws that reach the stator will short the windings
Centre tube is concentric; spin the bell by hand and feel for rub
Anodising is even, with no bare patches near the screw holes

parts.name: Stator
parts.role: The fixed electromagnet that pushes the rotor around.
parts.whatItDoes: The stator is a stack of thin steel sheets with copper wire wound around each of its twelve teeth. When the ESC switches current through the windings, each tooth becomes a magnet in turn and pulls the rotor magnets after it.
parts.whyItMatters: Thinner, better insulated laminations lose less power as heat. Tighter, more even windings give more torque from the same current. Together they decide how hot the motor runs and how long a battery lasts.
parts.material: Laminated silicon steel core with enamelled copper windings
buyingChecks: Lamination thickness is stated, ideally 0.2 mm or thinner
Winding wire temperature class is stated, 180 C or higher for hot climates
Phase resistance is close across all three phase pairs
No scraped enamel where the windings meet the tooth edges
Ask where the lamination steel is made; it is often not documented

checked: Lamination thickness as stated by the supplier
Winding wire class as stated on the wire declaration
notChecked: Lamination thickness, by our own measurement

parts.name: Phase lead wires
parts.role: Carry current from the ESC into the three phases of the winding.
parts.whatItDoes: Three silicone-insulated wires connect the winding ends to the ESC. Their gauge sets how much current they can carry before they heat up.
parts.whyItMatters: Undersized leads waste power and get hot. Stiff insulation cracks with vibration. A poor joint at the winding end is a common cause of a motor cutting out in flight.
buyingChecks: Gauge suits your peak current; 18 AWG is common up to about 40 A bursts
Insulation is silicone, not PVC
Length reaches your ESC without a joint
Strand count is high enough that the wire stays flexible

parts.name: Lower bearing
parts.role: Lets the shaft spin freely at the bottom of the motor.
parts.whatItDoes: A small sealed ball bearing pressed into the base tube. It keeps the shaft centred while letting it spin with very little friction.
parts.whyItMatters: Bearings are the part of a motor that wears out. Cheap or poorly fitted bearings get noisy, add vibration and eventually let the bell touch the stator.
parts.material: Chrome steel races and balls, rubber seals
buyingChecks: Bearing brand and size are stated, so you can source replacements
Spin the motor by hand; it should be smooth with no gritty feel
Ask whether bearings are pressed or glued in, which affects servicing

evidence.summary: Bearing markings read on the inspected sample.
checked: Brand marking and size code on both bearings
Supplier statement that the bearings are bought from a Japanese maker
notChecked: Whether the bearings are genuine, beyond the marking
Bearing life or noise under load

parts.name: Upper bearing
parts.role: Keeps the top of the shaft centred inside the stator.
parts.whatItDoes: The second ball bearing, seated at the top of the base tube. With the lower bearing it holds the shaft in line so the magnets stay a constant distance from the stator.
parts.whyItMatters: The upper bearing takes most of the side load from the propeller. If it wears first, the air gap between rotor and stator becomes uneven and efficiency drops.
parts.material: Chrome steel races and balls, rubber seals
buyingChecks: Same checks as the lower bearing
After a crash, check for play by rocking the bell sideways
Replacement bearings should be the same size and seal type

parts.name: Rotor magnets
parts.role: Fourteen permanent magnets that the stator pulls around.
parts.whatItDoes: Curved magnets are bonded in a ring inside the bell with alternating north and south poles. The stator's changing field pulls on them, which turns the bell and the propeller.
parts.whyItMatters: Magnet strength sets torque. Their temperature rating sets how hot the motor can run before they lose strength for good. A grade with an SH suffix holds up to about 150 C.
parts.material: Sintered NdFeB (neodymium iron boron), nickel coated
buyingChecks: Magnet grade is documented, including the temperature suffix
Ask for the magnet maker's certificate, not only the motor datasheet
Look for chipped coating; exposed NdFeB corrodes
Check that magnets are bonded, not only pressed in

parts.name: Bell housing
parts.role: The spinning outer shell that carries the magnets and the propeller.
parts.whatItDoes: The bell is the rotor's frame. The magnets are bonded inside it, the shaft is pressed into its top, and the open spokes pull air through the motor to cool the windings.
parts.whyItMatters: A stiff, well balanced bell keeps the magnets at a constant distance from the stator at full speed. The size of its spoke openings sets how much cooling air moves across the windings.
buyingChecks: Spin the bell and watch the rim for wobble
Check the bell is a single piece or that the top is firmly joined
Vent openings are clean, with no burrs near the windings

parts.name: Shaft
parts.role: Joins the spinning bell to the bearings and carries the propeller.
parts.whatItDoes: A hardened steel rod pressed into the bell. It runs down through both bearings, and its threaded top end takes the propeller nut.
parts.whyItMatters: A bent shaft is the most common damage after a crash and causes heavy vibration. Shaft diameter and thread must match your propeller and prop nut.
buyingChecks: Shaft and thread match your propeller hub
Ask whether spare shafts are sold separately
Check the thread direction for each motor position

parts.name: Retaining clip
parts.role: Stops the shaft and bell from pulling out of the base.
parts.whatItDoes: A small spring steel clip sits in a groove at the bottom of the shaft, under the base. It holds the rotor in place against the pull of the propeller.
parts.whyItMatters: If the clip is missing or loose, the propeller can lift the bell off in flight. It is a cheap part that is easy to lose during servicing.
buyingChecks: Check the clip is seated fully in its groove
Ask for spares with each order
Some motors use a screw instead; check which your servicing tools need
